result.title: CoRS: Fast Neural Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling via Composite Interval State Reuse
result.summary: Neural solvers for the Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) typically refresh graph representations and update feasibility after every operation--machine decision. However, only feasibility must remain exact at every step, whereas graph encoding is substantially more expensive and can potentially be refreshed less frequently. We present CoRS, which decouples them: an interval-level graph representation is reused across multiple sequential decisions, while a stepwise feasibility state is updated after every action. This two-timescale design amortizes graph encoding without parallelizing action generation or relaxing scheduling constraints. CoRS further develops a feasibility-preserving composite-interval decoding scheme with dynamic constraint tracking and boundary state synchronization, which reduces representation refresh frequency while maintaining continuous feasible schedule construction. Furthermore, to alleviate representation staleness caused by interval-level state reuse, CoRS introduces enhanced static features as a compensation mechanism. By providing more comprehensive structural information of the scheduling problem, these features improve the model's perception of overall problem characteristics. Extensive experiments on synthetic and multiple public FJSP benchmarks demonstrate that CoRS significantly reduces inference time while maintaining competitive solution quality, achieving favorable speed-quality trade-offs under tight wall-clock budgets and low-latency scenarios.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 Flexible Job-Shop 调度提出 CoRS：把昂贵的图编码改为区间级复用，仅对可行性状态逐步更新，并辅以复合区间解码与静态特征补偿表示陈旧，在保持解质量的同时降低推理耗时。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「表示低频刷新＋状态逐步精确更新」的双时间尺度设计与陈旧性补偿，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 缓存复用、更新频率与表示漂移的权衡。
